title: The previous clerk
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, lonely 1970s roadside motel at night in the rain, buzzing pink neon and sodium orange glow against deep blue darkness, wood paneling and worn carpet, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 3. The last night clerk finally told me what Room 9 is. 🛎️

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: every guest of Room 9 since 1964 checked in and never checked out. The newest name was Marcus's own.
scenes.image: an old guestbook open under a desk lamp, a man's hand pressed flat over the last page

scenes.narration: Mr. Dell said only one clerk ever lasted more than a month. Lorraine. Nineteen years on the night desk. She lives two towns over. She doesn't answer her phone.
scenes.image: an empty motel front desk at night, an old rotary phone ringing with nobody to answer it

scenes.narration: Marcus drove there on his day off. A small yellow house. Every curtain drawn. Every light on, at noon.
scenes.image: small yellow house on a quiet road at midday, every curtain drawn, every window glowing with lamplight

scenes.narration: Lorraine was about seventy. She looked at him through the screen door and said: who'd you give the key to?
scenes.image: older woman with silver hair and reading glasses peering through a screen door, suspicious and afraid

scenes.narration: She made tea she never drank. She kept her hands flat on the table so he wouldn't see them shake.
scenes.image: two cups of untouched tea on a kitchen table, an old woman's hands pressed flat beside them

scenes.narration: You think it's a room, she said. Bed. TV. Ice bucket. It isn't. Room 9 isn't a room. It's a waiting list.
scenes.image: close-up of the old woman's lined face in warm lamplight, eyes fixed and grave

scenes.narration: Everyone who signs the book is in line. The man in the raincoat comes to collect. He checks people in. Just not here.
scenes.image: a man in a grey raincoat walking away down a rainy motel walkway, seen from behind, neon reflections

scenes.narration: Marcus asked why she was never collected. Because I never let the book have my name, she said. You did.
scenes.image: an old woman pushing a cup across a table toward a young man, his face pale

scenes.narration: At the door she held his arm. Don't go back. And whatever he asks for, don't give it to him.
scenes.image: an elderly woman gripping a man's sleeve in a doorway, daylight behind them

scenes.narration: Driving home, Marcus passed the Bluebell. The whole motel was dark. Except one window.
scenes.image: dark roadside motel seen from a passing car at night, only one window at the end of the row glowing
